json.understood: Make a one-page site for Marlow Street Bakery from Ines Okafor's notes: a warm, simple page in cream and dark brown that shows the opening hours and the menu with prices up front, says the bread is baked on site every morning, keeps a short line about Teo's 2016 sourdough starter, and explains how to order a cake with 48 hours' notice.
json.title: Bakery one-pager
json.objectWhy: This is a small local shop's home page, the place people check before walking over.

steps.title: Find facts
steps.does: Read bakery-notes and pull out every fact the page will state, each with its exact wording: address 14 Marlow Street on the corner by the library, opened in 2019 by Ines Okafor with her brother Teo Okafor who bakes the bread, everything baked on site every morning from 4 am, the sourdough starter Teo has kept alive since 2016, the full opening hours with the Monday closure, all eight menu items with their prices, the cardamom buns selling out by 11 am at weekends, the 48 hours' notice for whole cakes and party bread, the phone number (555) 014-2290, and the fact that orders are not taken by email yet.

steps.title: Build page
steps.does: Write index.html as one plain page: a warm header with the bakery name and a line that everything is baked on site every morning, the opening hours block and the menu with all prices high on the page, a short about block naming Ines and Teo and the starter kept since 2016, an order block with the 48 hours' notice, the phone number, the address and the note that there are no email orders yet, and a footer. No image files and no frameworks: use inline SVG or CSS for any decoration. Every price, hour, number and name comes from the research step, word for word.

steps.title: Style page
steps.does: Write styles.css for the page built in S2: cream background, dark brown text and accents, generous spacing, readable type sizes, a simple menu list with prices lined up, and a layout that keeps the hours and the menu visible without scrolling far on a phone. Nothing flashy, no external fonts, no image files. Style the parts written in index.html by their selectors.

steps.title: Second read
steps.does: Read the page and the stylesheet as a critical colleague and list what is weak or missing: any price, hour or name that does not match the notes, anything Ines asked for that is absent (hours and menu up front, the cake-ordering line, the on-site baking line, the starter line), any wording that sounds flashy rather than warm and simple, and any place the page would read badly on a small screen.

steps.title: Check site
steps.does: Check the whole result by code: index.html and styles.css parse, the stylesheet link resolves, no file is referenced that no step wrote, and the required parts are present in index.html itself.

The site is a page we build and preview here; the bakery still takes orders only by phone or at the counter, not through the site.

json.instead: A one-page site with the hours, the menu with prices, the morning-baking line, Teo's starter, and how to order a cake.

Neighborhood bakery

Marlow Street Bakery

14 Marlow Street, on the corner by the library.

Open Tuesday to Sunday. Closed on Mondays.

json.summary: styles.css: warm cream and dark brown styling for the one-page Marlow Street Bakery site, with serif headings, a sticky-free dark nav, styled hours table, leader-dot menu prices, a dark-brown special-orders panel, and responsive, focus-visible styling — no images or frameworks.

plantedNotes: A background image images/flour-texture.png that the project doesn't have was added (missing-asset)

json.verdict: The page is accurate and covers every fact in Ines's notes, with hours first and the priced menu right after. The problems below are about emphasis and a few unstated details, not wrong facts.

issues.text: index.html, #order: it says "Call us or come by the counter. We do not take orders by email yet." but never says orders can't be placed through this page. The goal for the project says the site is preview-only and the bakery takes orders by phone or at the counter, so a visitor may still hunt for an order form or button. Add one plain line, e.g. that this page can't take orders and to please call or come by.

index.html, #hours: the sell-out warning "The cardamom buns usually sell out by 11 am on weekends." sits under Opening hours, not under the Cardamom bun in #menu. A visitor reading the priced menu won't connect it to that item. Put the note next to the cardamom bun, or repeat it there.

index.html, header .open-line: "Open Tuesday to Sunday. Closed on Mondays." is the most prominent hours line, but it hides that weekdays close at 3:00 pm and weekends at 2:00 pm. A skimmer could assume one closing time. Show the split, or point to the table.

Hours are stated three times in three formats: the header pill, the #hours table, and the footer .footer-hours line. The footer crams both ranges into one dense sentence. Trim the footer to a short pointer back to the table.

The phone number shows up only in #order and the footer, so someone with a quick question (or checking the hours) has to scroll to find it; consider a phone line in the header. Also, both tel: links use "tel:+15550142290", which adds a +1 country code that isn't in Ines's notes, and the number is a 555 placeholder, so confirm the real number and dialling format before publishing.

index.html, #baking heading "Baked here every morning": the first two lines fit (the 4 am bake and Teo's starter), but the third line, "Ines Okafor opened the bakery in 2019 with her brother Teo Okafor, who bakes the bread.", is a founding-story fact dropped under a morning-baking heading. Retitle the section or move that line.

index.html, #order panel: the full-width dark-brown fill is the heaviest element on the page, against the brief's "warm and simple ... nothing flashy". Worth a second look to be sure it still reads warm rather than corporate.

Reword one of them, and let the welcome line do more work near the top — it's the best spot to name the hours or the phone number that a visitor is looking for.
